title: point a drill at a target on the table
instruction: Pick up the drill and hold it with the chuck pointing straight down at the red dot.
context: Positioning a drill above a marked work location is a preparatory step in construction and maintenance. This task isolates grasping a handled tool and controlling its chuck axis and clearance above the work surface.
setup: Two 6-DoF I2RT YAM arms with parallel-jaw grippers are mounted 0.61 m apart, with bases at (0, 0.305, 0.75) m and (0, -0.305, 0.75) m. World X points forward from the arms, Y left, and Z up. Both arms start at joint angles [0, 1, 1, -0.6, 0, 0] radians with their grippers open, approximately 94 mm between the jaws. The stationary oak-colored tabletop is 1.10 x 1.30 m and 0.06 m thick, centred at (0.36, 0, 0.7175) m, with its top at Z = 0.7475 m. A cordless drill with plastic-housing and metal-chuck appearance, approximately 187 x 185 x 57 mm and mass 0.5 kg, rests on its side in front of the right arm. Its horizontal bounding-box centre is at (0.25, -0.30) m and its starting yaw is 90 degrees about world Z, with the chuck pointing approximately along world -Y. The target is a fixed red cylinder, 30 mm in diameter and 1 mm thick, centred at (0.30, -0.15, 0.7480) m. The station also contains a floor, a fixed overhead RGB camera and its stand behind the arms, and an RGB camera on each wrist. The drill is the only loose task object. Disable object-position jitter to reproduce this fixed starting layout.
scoring: Use the task_score evaluator. Lift clearance is the height of the lowest point of the drill mesh above the tabletop, computed from transformed support vertices. Tilt is the angle between the chuck axis and vertically downward. Aim error is the horizontal distance from the target-dot centre to the forward chuck-axis intersection with the tabletop plane. Award 1.0 and terminate successfully when lift clearance is strictly greater than 0.020 m, tilt is strictly less than 15 degrees, and aim error is strictly less than 0.040 m, with all three conditions maintained continuously for 1.0 second (20 consecutive control steps at 20 Hz). If full success is not reached, award partial credit from the final control step: 0.0 if no steps were executed or lift clearance is at most 0.020 m; 0.25 if lifted but tilt is at least 15 degrees; 0.50 if lifted with tilt below 15 degrees but aim error is at least 0.050 m; 0.75 if lifted with tilt below 15 degrees and aim error below 0.050 m. Partial credit has no hold requirement.
run_limit: 2,400 robot control steps at 20 Hz, equivalent to 120 seconds of simulation time per trial. A trial ends earlier if full success is reached. Inference and rendering can increase elapsed wall-clock time.
reset_notes: Use evaluation seed 0 and disable object-position jitter. Reset or restart the simulator to restore both arms to their ready poses with open grippers and return the drill to its initial pose. The table and marker are fixed; no objects are consumed or modified.
fidelity: Isaac Sim PhysX models rigid robot links, joint limits, gravity, drill grasping, collisions and friction at 240 Hz, with joint-position commands at 20 Hz. The drill uses the Arena power_drill USD asset as a single rigid body with total mass 0.5 kg. Contact parameters, surface-material properties and internal mass distribution are approximations rather than measurements of a particular physical drill. The table, target marker and camera stand are fixed colliders. Clearance uses support vertices extracted from the drill USD mesh, scaled and transformed with the measured object pose. Aiming uses the same model frame and scale for the chuck-axis direction and tip offset. The trigger, motor, chuck rotation, bit cutting, drilling forces, deformation and surface damage are not simulated; the task requires pointing above the dot, without drilling or touching the table.
